title: Attention & Memory: scratchpad notes and quick experiments
body:
Context: quick personal digest while prepping an internal brownbag on memory patterns for long-context LLMs. Keep this chaotic — actionable bits below.

Goals:
- Build 3 tiny repros to test caching+attention tradeoffs on sequence lengths 4k/16k/64k.
- Figure out tail latency behaviour when warming vs cold cache.
- Draft a one-pager for SE team on 'when to use prefix/KV caching vs chunked context retrieval'.

Papers/blogs I want to synthesize (quick bullets):
- Flash/Block attention variants: big win when tile sizes and memory bandwidth line up; important to benchmark with our runtime kernels (not just PyTorch baseline). Note: memory-bound for short sequences, compute-bound for very long ones.
- KV-MoE and sparse routing notes: routing overhead + memory amplification. Good for overall FLOP efficiency but tricky for batching. Keep as 'maybe' for Dedicated customers with predictable large throughput.
- Alibi / linear positional biases: lightweight for extrapolation, but watch for degraded alignment on instruction-following tasks (see evals section).
- Retrieval-augmented prefix: different failure modes than KV-cache; retrieval adds noisy tokens but is robust to cache staleness.

Quick takeaways (my opinions):
- For RLHF-style chat workloads (many short turns), aggressive KV prefix caching wins. Frequent cache invalidation is the bigger risk than space.
- For single massive context (>32k) from documents, chunking + retrieval on embeddings + dynamic rerank is often cheaper than a huge contiguous attention window.
- Quantized KV storage is underexplored: 8-bit storage for keys gives good memory savings with small perf hit. Worth 2-week microbenchmark.

Planned experiments (short checklist):
- [ ] microbench: measure token-p90/p99 for 4k/16k/64k with cold vs warm KV cache (model: 13B fp16, batch=1, seqs: synthetic).
- [ ] kernel compare: run Flash-like kernel vs baseline on our 80GB GPU; track memory bandwidth counters.
- [ ] quant-KV: prototype storing keys in int8, see downstream perplexity drift on a 1000-prompt eval set.
- [ ] batching stress: emulate 50 QPS with bursty arrival; evaluate batching latency SLOs and queueing behavior.

Experiment notes / hypotheses:
- Hypothesis A: warm KV cache reduces p99 by >40% for multi-turn chat where turn tokens > 256.
- Hypothesis B: quantized keys will not increase generation token error rate by more than 1.5% for 8-bit symmetric quant.

Mini eval checklist (quick):
- Dataset: 500 multi-turn dialogues sampled from internal chat-prod (mask any PII).
- Metrics: p50/p90/p99 latency, tokens/sec, downstream answer accuracy on 20-shot retrieval QA, 10-shot summarization ROUGE.

Open questions to ask on brownbag:
- How often do teams want deterministic outputs vs best-effort cost savings (i.e., cache warming windows)?
- Is there appetite for a shared quantized KV-store across models in the same tenant?

Notes from Slack/threads: 
- @owen: "We saw a regression when we applied per-layer quant to cache keys in a canary — flashing token repeats for certain prompts." Need to replicate.
- @sophia: suggested a synthetic corpus with repeated prefixes to stress cache correctness. Good idea.

Draft one-pager outline (for product/solutions):
- Problem statement: growing customer demand for long context with SLOs.
- Options: large-window attention vs chunked retrieval vs KV caching vs hybrid.
- Tradeoffs: cost, latency, determinism, implementation complexity.
- Recommendation: default to KV caching for interactive chat workloads; default to retrieval+chunking for document ingestion; surface quantized-kv as opt-in.

Quick command snippets (for myself):
- synthetic data create: python tools/gen_synthetic.py --turns 50 --seq-len 4096 --seed 42
- perf run: ./bench/run_inference --model 13b --seq 16384 --batch 1 --kernel flash --kv-cache warm

To-dos after brownbag:
- Make a small benchmark repo with reproducible scripts + cloud VM snapshot. (Assign to me).
- Sync with runtime team on kernel instrumentation points (bandwidth, L2 hits).
- Prototype int8-kv and run small eval.

Random thoughts / heuristics for notes app:
- If customer needs consistent tokenization-based context across rollouts, pin the cache serialization format in the model spec.
- Expose a "cache-warmth" metric (0-1) on console so customers can reason about cold starts.

End of scratchpad — will tidy into a proper doc once experiments return numbers.
summary: Personal scratchpad: notes on attention/memory patterns for long-context LLMs, list of papers to synthesize, hypotheses, experiment checklist, draft one-pager outline and next steps.
